THIS WEEK IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT

Marathon County set new zoning rules for battery storage and data centers and punted a contentious wind energy resolution back to committee, while Wausau's Finance Committee advanced key funding items including a tax increment bond for the Foundry on Third development.

  • Marathon County adopted a 500-foot setback requirement for battery energy storage systems and a temporary moratorium on data centers, and referred the Hub City Wind project resolution back to the Executive Committee for a clearer recommendation at September's meeting.
  • The Wausau Finance Committee approved a tax increment revenue bond for the Foundry on Third development and adopted a budget workshop calendar with four sessions beginning October 5 at 6:30 p.m.
  • The Wausau Board of Public Works approved Clark Dietz to conduct a sanitary sewer capacity assessment and authorized over $1.2 million in combined pay estimates for lead service line replacement and Stark Street construction.
  • The Wausau Police & Fire Commission launched a deputy chief promotional process — applications open in September, with a decision expected at the December commission meeting — framed as early succession planning for the police chief role.
  • The Village of Weston approved a $1.29 million waterworks revenue bond and held its first joint board-finance budget workshop in several years, keeping trustee compensation flat at $7,200 for the 2027–2029 term.
  • Kronenwetter's Village Board is set to vote on accepting the Village Clerk's resignation at a special meeting called for August 27.

Coming up: The Wausau Committee of the Whole meets Wednesday, September 2 at 5:30 p.m. — worth watching given the range of city business in play — and the City's Public Health & Safety Committee meets the same evening at 5:00 p.m. Marathon County's Health & Human Services Committee meets Thursday, September 3 at 5:00 p.m.
